$comment: Keyless vendors that were MEASURED not to answer. The gateway serves ~77 models that need no key at all and publishes no health for any of them - `tllm` reports active:true and then answers HTTP 403 - so the only honest signal is a real completion. The app hides these vendors' models from the picker, never retries onto them, and always offers a one-click way to see them anyway. Re-measure with `node scripts/check-keyless-health.mjs`, which prints any vendor that has recovered or newly died.
$commentMethod: Each verdict is 5 models per vendor, one at a time, 25 s apart, max_tokens 64. All three of those numbers are load-bearing. The gateway caches ONE upstream failure and replays it onto that vendor's other models for ~90 s, so back-to-back attempts can be a single failure counted five times. And a 8-token budget lets a reasoning model spend everything thinking and return an empty string: the first pass condemned `oc` for exactly that, and at 64 tokens `oc/big-pickle` answered "OK" straight away. A vendor is only listed here if EVERY model tried refused.
$commentScope: `openrouter`, `no-think` and `auto` are deliberately not measured. The first two are namespaces over a connection the reader paid for, and `auto` is the gateway's own routing combo that resolves to some other model at call time.
$commentFinding: Measured 2026-09-03: of the 9 keyless vendors on offer, 8 are dead and 1 works. 71 of the 77 keyless models cannot answer. `oc` (6 models) is the entire working free pool. That is the real state of this product without a key, and it is why the provider-key flow is the product rather than a nicety.
